newsitem.title: ITALY: Budget to ensure Italy in at EMU start - Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Budget to ensure Italy in at EMU start - Prodi.

text.p: The 1997 budget will ensure Italy becomes a founder member of planned European economic and monetary union (EMU), Prime Minister Romano Prodi told a news conference on Friday.

Prodi said the heart of the budget would raise between 36-37 trillion lire with additional funds coming from a one-off "Euro tax". He said the cabinet meeting, called to approve the package which has lasted for over 10 hours, would resume later on Friday to put finishing touches to the draft law.
Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi told the same news conference that two thirds of the budget would be made up of spending cuts and one third from fresh revenues.
A further 12 trillion lire would be sliced from the public sector deficit by as yet undefined "treasury operations".
Ciampi added that the package would bring the country credibility and added that this in turn should spark a fall in interest rates.
Prodi said all the centre-left government's allies supported the budget package which has to be approved by parliament before the end of December. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
